rv.q: This is richly imaginative writing that marks Yew out as a playwright of tantalising promise.
She makes an already striking play about the push and pull between cultural tradition and independence all the more compelling.
For a first-time playwright, The Hungry Ghost is a confident and wonderfully original piece of writing, and one that leaves its audience hungry for whatever Yew serves up next.
It’s enjoyable and worth seeing – expect to laugh a lot – but it isn’t flawless.
Each individual element of the production is executed with moments of brilliance – but with an underlying predictability, it does leave you wanting more.
Although The Hungry Ghost has an unnecessary interval, it is an original and successful piece of new writing 贊成.
The Hungry Ghost as a production simply gets everything right.
It’s warm, hilariously funny and heartfelt.
For horror with real heart, The Hungry Ghost is the perfect addition to your spooky season lineup this October.
Everything about The Hungry Ghost feels exciting.
Comedy is the key, producing a piece with a gentle touch that leaves the audience feeling full.
I do believe that anyone with an open mind and a love for theatre should hail this play as the triumph that it is.

Ailin Conant’s 100-miles-per-hour direction makes this an utter thrill to watch, and gives weight to those rare moments of silence – where Girl realises she’s possessed, and her mother gives a scathing assessment of how messy her life is.
What starts as a chaotic comedy about sex, food and a troublesome spirit becomes a surprisingly moving story about culture, queerness and belonging.
The Ghost's departure from Girl leaves a sense of a story well rounded and well told, though a little more time with the Ghost's life before she became a ghost might have been even more satisfying.
The Hungry Ghost is a true example of why to go to the theatre: with its unique story and excellent production, its compelling from start to finish and leaves you hungry for more.
This is an eye-popping, delightfully delirious debut work.
The Hungry Ghost is a play that is culturally rich and fast-paced... highly imaginative and successfully sustains its ideas, and you won't see anything else quite like it.
It's actually a bloody good time at the theatre!

Mei Mac also showcases unparallel acting capacity, performing the girl as well as all the other human characters: her mother, her white female manager, a male police officer and her Scottish girlfriend.
In Ailin Conant's production this is a funny, frantic and sometimes moving show - it doesn't really lean into the horror aspect much but it does flash a couple of creepy images along the way.
The Hungry Ghost is therefore an enjoyable and occasionally very funny production, with particularly strong performances, sound and physicality.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive, culturally-rich debut as a wildly funny supernatural romcom that blends Chinese folklore with queer romance. Mei Mac's performance earns raves, though some note the final act falters and cultural specificity may challenge uninitiated audiences.
